security_audit.summary: Most static backtick and URL findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and official AWS reference links. Real risk remains because the skill presents AWS CLI and boto3 cleanup actions that can delete volumes, delete snapshots, release public IPs, and inventory multiple accounts.

remediation.issue: Destructive AWS cleanup actions are presented without mandatory guardrails.
remediation.suggestion: Make dry-run the default, require explicit approval, add tag and account allowlists, require final snapshots, and document rollback steps before any delete or release action.

remediation.issue: Risk metadata declares the skill safe despite destructive cloud operations.
remediation.suggestion: Update the declared risk level and document required least-privilege IAM permissions for discovery and cleanup modes.

remediation.issue: Cross-account examples can inventory broad AWS Organizations environments.
remediation.suggestion: Scope examples to named accounts, regions, profiles, and tags, and require read-only discovery before cross-account cleanup.

content.user_title: Reduce AWS Waste with Cleanup Workflows
content.value_statement: Unused AWS resources create recurring cloud spend and operational clutter. This skill helps teams find cleanup candidates, estimate savings, and plan safer AWS cleanup workflows.
actual_capabilities: Identifies common cleanup targets, including unattached EBS volumes, old snapshots, unused Elastic IPs, load balancers, NAT gateways, and ENIs.
Provides dry-run shell examples for EBS volumes, old snapshots, and Elastic IP cleanup.
Shows S3 lifecycle policy setup for storage transitions, version expiration, and incomplete multipart upload cleanup.
Includes a Python savings calculator for unattached EBS volumes and unused Elastic IPs.
Outlines an AWS Lambda example for scheduled cleanup of unattached volumes.
Documents cleanup phases, safety checks, verification steps, and rollback planning.
limitations: Requires valid AWS credentials, IAM permissions, and AWS CLI or boto3 setup.
Does not automatically prove ownership, compliance retention needs, or hidden application dependencies.
Destructive examples must be reviewed before use in production environments.
AWS prices and service behavior can change, so savings estimates need current pricing checks.

use_cases.title: Audit Orphaned Cloud Resources
use_cases.description: Find unused AWS resources and prepare a reviewed cleanup list before maintenance windows.

use_cases.title: Estimate Cleanup Savings
use_cases.description: Turn resource inventory into monthly and annual savings estimates for cost review meetings.

use_cases.title: Plan Recurring Cleanup Operations
use_cases.description: Design scheduled discovery, lifecycle policies, approvals, and verification steps for platform teams.

prompt_templates.title: Find Cleanup Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-cost-cleanup to list possible unused AWS resources in my account. Start with read-only discovery and explain what each resource type means.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate Monthly Savings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-cost-cleanup to estimate monthly savings from unattached EBS volumes, old snapshots, and unused Elastic IPs. Include assumptions and review notes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Safe Cleanup Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-cost-cleanup to create a production cleanup plan with dry-run steps, owner approval, backup checks, rollback steps, and verification tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Cross-Account Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use aws-cost-cleanup to design a cross-account cleanup workflow for AWS Organizations. Scope it by account, region, tag, IAM role, approval gate, and audit log.

output_examples.input: Find unused AWS resources and estimate monthly savings.
output_examples.output: A report listing unattached EBS volumes, old snapshots, unused Elastic IPs, estimated monthly savings, and review notes for each category.

output_examples.input: Create a production cleanup plan for old snapshots.
output_examples.output: A phased plan with discovery, owner validation, compliance checks, approval, dry-run execution, rollback contacts, and post-cleanup verification.

output_examples.input: Set up S3 lifecycle cleanup for stale objects.
output_examples.output: A lifecycle policy plan covering storage transitions, noncurrent version cleanup, incomplete upload cleanup, and monitoring checks.

best_practices: Start with read-only discovery and dry-run output before any destructive cleanup.
Scope cleanup by account, region, tags, owner, and environment.
Keep backups, audit logs, approvals, and rollback procedures for every cleanup run.
anti_patterns: Running generated delete commands with broad administrator permissions and no review.
Deleting snapshots or volumes based only on age without checking owners and retention rules.
Scheduling cleanup automation before validating dependencies, tags, backups, and alerts.

faq.question: Does this skill run AWS commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. A user or agent must decide when to run commands with AWS credentials.

faq.question: Can it delete production resources?
faq.answer: Yes, if destructive examples are used with cleanup permissions. Review every command and use least privilege before production use.

faq.question: What permissions are needed?
faq.answer: Read-only IAM permissions are enough for discovery. Cleanup requires service-specific delete or release permissions.

faq.question: Does it replace AWS Cost Explorer?
faq.answer: No. It complements billing tools by turning resource inventory into cleanup candidates and workflow steps.

faq.question: How should teams use it safely?
faq.answer: Run discovery first, identify owners, confirm dependencies, take backups, and require approval for destructive actions.

faq.question: Does it support multiple AWS accounts?
faq.answer: It includes an AWS Organizations example, but cross-account use needs explicit profiles, scopes, and controls.
